entry.title: PARASOMA
entry.summary:
PARASOMA is a research project we’re developing at NastPlas on the body an organism would have if it were formed by two biological systems in a stable association. What interests us is the boundary between them: one region densifies because it has to bear tension, another stretches into a membrane, an interface thickens until it becomes a compartment.
We start from documented phenomena (lichenization, extracellular matrix, endosymbiosis, differential growth, structural color) and turn them into organizational rules. What comes out of those rules is speculation, and we keep it carefully separate from what has been established. None of these forms exist, but each one should be explainable.
There are 21 open series. Each starts from a hypothesis, carries its own risk and its own palette, and we discard a lot.
As the research moved forward, the rules started to feel too limited for a still image. So we developed two applications that are part of the project.

entry.title: Stori
entry.summary: Proyecto por Niklas Rosén con 41 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Niklas Rosén, Gustav Nordebrink

Stori
Stori is reimagining one of pregnancy's most exciting early moments. With a simple at-home blood test, parents can discover their baby's gender from as early as five weeks — turning a clinical process into a private, personal experience designed to be shared and remembered. Based in the US, Stori combines laboratory-grade accuracy with a warm, intuitive product experience, meeting expectant parents at the very beginning of their story.

Since early 2025, we have worked closely with the Stori team to build the brand from the ground up. The central strategic goal has been to create a warm and inviting atmosphere that sets Stori apart in a category defined by clinical expression. Natural light, skin and touch form the visual core, paired with an editorial typographic voice that treats the science of early pregnancy as something to be read rather than reported. Our work spans brand identity, packaging, website and digital product, communication and social media, along with a system of templates for print and various digital touchpoints. The result is a cohesive identity with a tone that is intimate rather than clinical: a design language built to carry Stori from first launch to a growing international audience.

entry.title: Kokkeløren
entry.summary: Proyecto por OlssønBarbieri : ) con 35 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): OlssønBarbieri : )

Kokkeløren (loosely translating little chef) is a small-scale challenger brand in the booming meal subscription service, competing with the big industry.
As the only meal-kit provider in Norway offering local produce and sauces and condiments made by their own chefs, Kokkeløren stands out with a clear value proposition in the category. In addition to communicating their close relationships with local suppliers and producers, we saw the potential for expanding their storytelling, creating a more unique experience, and demonstrating the brand investment in their community by supporting a more resilient local food system.​​​​​​​
Meal subscription services – the concept of ingredients, individually portioned up for cooking meals delivered at home – is booming. They are a convenient way to make evening meals without the hassle of planning recipes and visiting the supermarket.
Three meals are delivered each week with portioned ingredients and easy instructions for cooking. The recipes take little time to prepare and the results are impressive thanks to chefs effort behind each recipe and sauces. It’s a step up from ready-meals as the food is prepared by hand, giving people the pleasure of cooking it.
These meal-kits are made to empower people to cook tasty and nourishing meals at home, with the best ingredients, providing a sense of mastering in the kitchen.
Our goal was to elevate the new branding and packaging to align with the high-end product and experience they offer, creating a more emotional connection with the brand. To align the visual narrative with the qualities Kokkeløren represent, we created an energetic and flexible system for communication, with a touch of nostalgia embodied in the chef-mascot, positioning Kokkeløren as a more contemporary and friendly brand offering a stronger connection to a service that many people experience several times a week.
The subscription meal-kit comes in two sizes, for 2 and 4 people, and is delivered in refrigerated cars, removing the need for ice bags, in an effort to minimize waste and optimize space. We also introduced numbered paper bags to organise each dinner in the fridge, extending the unboxing experience.
The smaller dinner-kits for two people come in custom-designed boxes with sleeves, and are sold in retail. Observing the ready-to-eat category language, we saw an opportunity to provide a more memorable, premium and fun experience, clarifying Kokkeløren´s position as a quality-focused meal-kit provider, and creating a stronger synergy between the retail and subscription experience.
Each sleeve has a recipe colour, inspired by the flavour profile of the recipes, their ingredients and/or origin. The trapezoidal prism shape offers a unique and structurally strong box with a memorable presence in retail, with proportions that are good to hold and handle. The sleeves are printed on both sides, completed with a step-by-step recipe on the back, and a tear-off to open.
The concept also introduces a wide colour palette and a fresh take on photography to better echo the wide selection of food cultures and complex flavours found in Kokkeløren’s recipes.
The strategic goal for the redesign is to elevate the branding and packaging to align with the taste experience that Kokkeløren offers, catering to consumers looking for a more meaningful and emotional connection to what they eat, supporting brands that nurture a growing network of small-scale and local producers.
While maintaining a strong synergy to the subscription service, we apply a bolder use of colour and an extended palette, combining photography and illustration to help clarify the product category and to offer a friendly, highly crafted and joyful experience.
Different templates were created to support the communication of each dinner-kit and the weekly meal subscription to highlight the ingredients, showing the making, costumers feedback and other relevant info about the dishes.
Valizas with its fun and flow-y appearance makes t​​​​​​​his typeface one of a kind with a unique and cheerful expression. Each character perfectly balance contemporary crispness with a touch of nostalgia, making it into a very food-friendly choice. The contrasts also reminds of a calligrafic style adding a human touch that is often hard to find in a sans serif typography.

entry.title: Centro de Arte Alberto Carneiro
entry.summary: Proyecto por united by con 26 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): united by, Maria Jorge, Diana Gaspar, Margarida Ferreira Silva, João Ventura


Centro de Arte Alberto Carneiro          Visual Identity, Editorial            2021 & 2026

The Centro de Arte Alberto Carneiro in Santo Tirso is a municipal initiative dedicated to the preservation, research, and promotion of contemporary art. The sculptor Alberto Carneiro holds a significant place in the cultural identity of the municipality, not only through the presence of his works throughout the city, but also through his pivotal role in initiating an ambitious public art programme that ultimately laid the foundations for the Museu Internacional de Escultura Contemporânea in Santo Tirso.
The visual identity draws inspiration from the verticality, rhythm, and organic forms that define Carneiro’s artistic practice. Its adaptable, organic character reflects both the sculptural language of the artist and his deep connection to the natural world. Designed to be flexible and expressive, the logo establishes a visual language that can evolve across different applications while maintaining a strong and distinctive identity.
In the centre’s communication materials, photography plays a central role. Images of artworks should preferably feature white backgrounds or be isolated from their original settings, allowing them to integrate seamlessly with the logo. This approach creates a cohesive visual composition in which the artworks and the identity coexist harmoniously, reinforcing the connection between the centre, the artist’s work, and the natural forms that inspire it.

Seeper came to us with almost 30 years of history creating immersive experiences through storytelling, technology and human connection. Their work had evolved, but their brand no longer reflected the creativity, scale or sophistication of the studio. The challenge was to change that perception while preserving the personality and heritage they had built.

Working closely with the team, we translated their positioning as Spatial Storytellers into a refreshed identity, expressive art direction and a flexible visual system. Bold typography, spatial graphics and dreamlike imagery gave the brand a distinctive voice, with enough range to step back and let their projects lead. Templates and guidelines gave the team the tools to take ownership and keep developing the brand.

Art Book「 Living Through the Seasons, Sometimes Thinking of Time」
2026

In this book, I have created illustrations inspired by the annual events, customs, and landscapes of Japan, where I live. I have also included illustrations about my parakeet, who lived with me for eleven years and passed away last year.
Since I live in Japan, many of the illustrations are rooted in Japanese culture. However, my intention was not simply to introduce or celebrate Japanese culture. Rather, I drew them with the thought that every place in the world must have its own familiar scenes and memories that people who grew up there carry with them.
I would be happy if these illustrations bring to mind your own hometown or evoke some of your own fond memories.

作品集「季節のなかで暮らすとき、ときどき月日を思ったり」2026

この作品集では、私が暮らす日本の一年の行事や風習、景色を意識して描きました。また、11年間一緒に暮らし、昨年亡くなったインコのことも描いています。
日本に住んでいるので、日本の文化を題材にした作品が多くなりましたが、日本の文化の良さを伝えたいというより、どこの国にも、その土地で暮らした人だけが思い出せるような懐かしい風景や記憶があるのだろうと思いながら描きました。
この絵を見て、それぞれの故郷や懐かしい記憶を思い出してもらえたらうれしいです。

A study of silence, intimacy and the spaces that bring us together.

Through minimal compositions and muted blue tones, this series explores the silent relationships between living forms, leaving space for emotion, imagination and the poetry of what remains unspoken.
Sometimes, what connects us is not what we share, but the space we leave for one another.
